rev-mv2zzd3g-019dc185.summary:
Technical review of rework-1 (sub-mv2zoxlo-019effce: 14 changed files plus the submission and followups.md), against the resolution conditions I wrote in rev-mv2zb2wy-019ac65d for TR-C-2, SEC-C-2 and SEC-C-3. Every check below ran after the submission, on the final tree (no project file changed since: 14 files differ from the claim base 4bfc13a1, exactly the listed artifacts).

Baseline:
- npm test: 821 tests, 805 pass, 10 skipped, 6 todo, 0 fail; NFR5 p95 54.8 ms over 2578 calls (ev:ev-mv2zrmza-016c0e05).
- npm run test:browser: 3/3 (ev:ev-mv2zrq4r-01ae051a).
- Artifacts equal the changes since 4bfc13a1, every sha256 matches, all inside the rework's ownership (ev:ev-mv2zv70k-01ca6173).
- The tests falsify: copied onto the pre-rework source they fail 19 times (TR-C-2 2, SEC-C-2 4, SEC-C-3 8 named failures) and pass 123/123 on the final tree (ev:ev-mv2zwsx9-012d555f).

My probes:
- General limit (ev:ev-mv2zt14w-01460430). The 301st call gets 429 general with Retry-After 60, and a refusal writes no row. Public routes and anonymous 401s are not counted. Plan and general keys are separate both ways (11 plan calls: plan rows +10, the 11th 429 plan while general passes). Only u:<id> and plan:u:<id> keys exist. With busy_timeout 0 and a held write lock, the answer is 503 DB_BUSY with Retry-After 1, never 500. The config bounds are refused by name and take effect.
- Across two processes: 120 concurrent calls of one user against limit 50 give exactly 50 passes, 70 refusals and 50 rows, in 3 rounds (ev:ev-mv2zxqy5-012a72ba).
- The phase-C probes still hold on this tree:
  - throttles, where the /64 is now one key and the 6th failure is refused (ev:ev-mv2ztesg-01b08c7d);
  - the RBAC matrix (ev:ev-mv2ztfq3-01364574);
  - the two-process reserve race (ev:ev-mv2ztoiz-01964725);
  - the 3 x 800-step random walk, where the limit broke no step (ev:ev-mv2zuvqn-014b7da3).

Error order is now Origin -> session (401) -> general limit (429) -> role (403) -> CSRF token (403). I accept the 429 between authentication and authorization: it keys on the user and bounds a signed-in client's probing. The signature-policy route returns before the limiter.

The security review (rework-1-security-1.md: no blocking or major) is folded in with its ids: SEC-R-1 minor, SEC-R-2..4 info; I agree with each severity. Decision: approve.

findings.title: Every authenticated request, reads included, now takes the SQLite write lock, so a held write lock turns signed-in reads into 503 DB_BUSY
findings.detail: general-limit.js runs a BEGIN IMMEDIATE on every non-public call. Before the rework, a signed-in GET only read through WAL, and the session touch deliberately tolerates busy. My G5 shows the mapping is correct (503 DB_BUSY with Retry-After 1, no 500, nothing counted); security's R3 shows the public session read still answers 200 (ev:ev-mv2zuhm9-0195be55). The effect is availability only. It grows once e4 adds a background writer (the reconciler), and every page poll is a counted write.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the orchestrator assigns it, to FU-20's owner or the next src/auth rework (backend-engineer). Resolved when, before e4's reconciler is dispatched, take() fails open for GET and HEAD on a busy error with one log line (state-changing methods stay fail-closed), and a test with test/helpers/lock-holder.js shows a signed-in GET answering 200 under a held write lock while a POST answers 503 DB_BUSY.

A cross-site fetch with credentials carried no cookie and counted nothing. At 300 per minute this needs about 300 popups a minute, so it is info.

resolvedFindings.resolution: Condition met. src/config.js parses RS_PLAN_RATE_LIMIT (1-1000, default 10) and RS_PLAN_RATE_WINDOW_MIN (1-1440, default 10) into planRateLimit and planRateWindowMin, which createApp reads. Both are in .env.example, and the env-example scan is green. Out-of-range values are refused by name; my G6 shows the bounds and the refusals. The bounds tests are named TR-C-2 rather than RISK-19, which I accept; the RISK-19 tests still cover the limit. Both TR-C-2 tests fail on the pre-rework source and pass now.

Condition met. throttleKey() maps IPv6 to its /64 for the sign-in and register throttles, for both the socket address and the trusted last X-Forwarded-For hop. IPv4 and ::ffff: (dotted and hex) keep their IPv4 key. Named tests show 5 failures over 5 addresses of one /64 making the 6th get 429 signin_pair, the register throttle counting a /64 once, and other prefixes and IPv4 staying separate. My throttle probe now shows the 6th failure from one /64 refused, with T8, SEC-1, SEC-9 and F-TR-17 unchanged. The SEC-C-2 tests fail on the pre-rework source. Security's R1 confirms 12 spellings.

Condition met, both points.
(1) The access hook counts every signed-in, non-public call in rate_events (kind general, key u:<id>); delete, count and insert run in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
- The 301st call gets 429 RATE_LIMITED, details.limit general, Retry-After.
- plan:u:<id> keys are never counted, and the two counts are separate both ways.
- Two processes never overshoot (50 of 120 concurrent calls pass, 3 rounds).
- A named test exists, and NFR5 p95 is 54.8 ms.
(2) A confirm equal to the latest version returns it without inserting a row. The engineer's stricter rule also requires equal derived provenance, which still bounds the flood (security's R2: 300 identical confirms wrote 0 rows).
The SEC-C-3 tests fail on the pre-rework source. The regression it introduced is SEC-R-1 (minor).

ho-mv1hk3zz-01649535.completedWork: REWORK after phase B review rev-mv1hc5zg-01a3fc75. PB-1 (blocking), root cause: on a fresh database file, PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL needs an exclusive lock. When another process holds or awaits a write lock while this connection holds a shared one, waiting could deadlock, so SQLite returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately and never calls the busy handler, so busy_timeout does not help. Reproduced with the reviewer's script (ev:ev-mv1hf138-016b38f3: 3 of 40 sequential runs failed with 'database is locked'; the script always exits 0, so the counts are the result) and with a minimal probe (.eccode/drafts/b1-pb1-probe.mjs, error code 5 from the WAL switch, about 1 in 180 opens). Fix in src/db/connection.js: openDb reads the journal mode first and switches only when the file is not WAL, and both that step and the later pragmas run under retryWhileBusy, a bounded back-off (2 ms doubling to 50 ms with jitter) on SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED up to max(busyTimeoutMs, 1000 ms), after which the busy error is rethrown; the handle is closed on failure. New test/unit/db/open-race.test.js (all named PB-1): retry unit tests, bounded give-up against a real lock-holder process, success when the holder releases, and a stress of 25 rounds x 4 processes on a fresh file. The same reproduction command now shows 0 failures in 160 runs (ev:ev-mv1hidob-01eb30b6); six more stress runs also passed; npm test passes 370/370 (ev:ev-mv1hjizn-013960db); the declared verification command passes with 177 tests (ev:ev-mv1hj5be-01ed33dd). ho-mv1jewhq-01c5bca8.completedWork: Algorithm (new src/domain/search.js, used by planner.js): the search enumerates offer SUBSETS within the pickup cap, smallest first, and solves each subset's covering problem exactly by bounded depth-first search. Pickups, plan-ready time and the supplier-code string depend on the subset alone, so inside a subset only total and vector matter. Pruning is valid and exact: (1) only irredundant plans are enumerated (the optimum is always irredundant: dropping a bundle never raises total, pickups or ready time and gives a smaller vector; the forced offer of a cheapest-cover query is exempt); (2) multiplicities are looped only inside the window [kLo, kHi] that the remaining demand allows; (3) a fractional-knapsack lower bound per dimension (mandatory later bundles, prep fees of unused suppliers, tax-rate scaling less one cent of rounding per touched order) cuts subtrees above the budget or the K-th best plan; (4) ascending canonical vector order lets a subtree that can only tie the K-th best of the same subset be cut, which removes equal-cost plateaus; (5) when no supplier has two members, a dominance table keyed by (position, cups, lids) keeps the K cheapest prefixes per state. Subsets are pre-filtered by a cheap root bound (cover floor plus prep sums). For infeasible requests the cheapest unconstrained cover answers every offer it uses, and any other offer is searched with that cover plus one bundle as its starting incumbent. Results: reproduction (stock 100, 10,000 cups, budget USD 100,000, maxPickups 5) now returns A at 301,000 cents in 0.1 ms, same as maxPickups 1. Sweep: 5,400 inputs, no PLANNER_LIMIT, worst single call 21.5 ms (was 237-305 ms with refusals). Stress (draft b2-planner-stress.mjs): 8,000 seeded-shape inputs with availability up to 100,000, quantities up to 100,000, differing cup/lid quantities and tax: worst 9.7 ms, no limit; 3,000 random-priced 12-offer catalogs: worst 36 ms; 3,000 catalogs with several offers per supplier: worst 23 ms. Tests added: planner-oracle.property.test.js gains (a) brute-force oracle on larger stock (availability up to 7, 100 catalogs), (b) tie-heavy catalogs against the oracle (equal prices, prep fees, ready times, several offers per supplier, 120 catalogs), (c) identical tied offers of one supplier, (d) 250 medium catalogs (availability up to 12, up to 6 offers, quantities up to 3000) against the frozen slow exact reference test/unit/domain/helpers/reference-planner.js, comparing the whole output; planner-fixture.test.js replaces the old absurd-input test with 'SEC-B-1: huge stock and quantity are solved exactly' (12 offers of single cups, 100,000 each, solved in well under 1 s) and a guard test of the node cap through search(..., {maxNodes}); test/timing/planner-sec-b1.test.js has the named test, a 1,008-call grid over the seeded shape (stock 1..100,000, quantity 100..100,000, no PLANNER_LIMIT, each < 100 ms, p95 < 20 ms) and 150 random 12-offer catalogs (each < 250 ms). A mutation (pruning ties across different subsets) was caught by the reference comparison and reverted. The earlier suites (RS-06..RS-11, 500-catalog oracle property, derive totality, states, money, time, explain, NFR5) pass unchanged.
remainingIssues: PLANNER_LIMIT (2,000,000 nodes per search, about 150 ms) is still a real guard, not an unreachable one. It is not reached by the seeded catalog shape, by random-priced catalogs of up to 12 offers, or by catalogs with several offers per supplier within the API ranges (evidence above). It CAN still be reached, and calls can take 150-400 ms (up to about 800 ms when several searches hit it), by deliberately tie-laden catalogs: several suppliers whose bundles of different size cost the same per bundle, quantity of about 50,000 or more, and especially a non-zero tax rate (rounding noise defeats tie pruning); and by catalogs whose bundles hold different numbers of cups and lids (not reachable through the API, which only seeds equal counts) at quantity 100,000. A supplier can set equal prices through PATCH, so this is reachable in principle; exactness for those needs an integer DP over coverage that I did not build in this round. Recommended in c2 regardless: map PlannerLimitError (RangeError, code PLANNER_LIMIT) to a typed 422/503, and add the per-customer rate limit on POST /api/requests/:id/plan and on re-plan drains that the security draft asks for (item 3 of its resolution).

Contract notes for d3 (src/services/extraction.js and src/main.js): (1) gate = createGate({db, clock, limits: gateLimitsFromConfig(config)}); the gate reads config fields modelDailyBudgetMicroUsd, modelCallCapMicroUsd, fakeModelCostMicroUsd (integers, preferred) and falls back to the existing modelDailyBudgetUsd, modelCallCapUsd, fakeModelCostUsd; modelCustomerDailyShare is already parsed (default 0.2). d3 may add the three micro fields to config.js with toMicroUsd(raw env string), or leave config.js unchanged; both work. (2) Call order: gate.takeRate(customerId) on every image upload; extraction = gate.run({customerId, requestId, call: () => provider.extract({text, image, signal})}) which takes the rate, reserves the cap, calls outside any transaction, settles with usage.costMicroUsd (or costUsd) and refunds on a thrown error. A refusal throws a domain AppError (429 RATE_LIMITED details.limit extract_upload|model_concurrency with headers['Retry-After'], or 503 MODEL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED details.scope global|customer) that the HTTP layer adopts via adoptAppError; d3 stores the degraded row in a separate transaction. (3) The fake takes faults: () => null|'timeout'|'invalid_json'|'schema_invalid'|'error' (a 'fake_model:' prefix is accepted); d3 must read and decrement the fake_model:* row of fault_flags and return the fault name, because adapters never touch service tables. (4) createFakeProvider({costMicroUsd}) takes integer micro-dollars: pass toMicroUsd(config.fakeModelCostUsd). (5) On ProviderError use toDegraded(err) for {schemaOk:false, degraded:true, errorCode, output: all unknown}. (6) validateExtraction(output, {text, imageNumbers}) rejects ungrounded output (provider adapters should call parseAndValidate with the request text); the spec's post-validation normalisation (downgrade to unknown, ranges, image wording stripping, non-USD budget) stays in services/extraction.js and is not implemented here. (7) renderQuestions(output.questions) gives the server-templated Question[].

Contract notes for d2: the fake image map is keyed by sha256 hex of the image bytes (not by an image id); entry shape {fields:{<name>:{value,wording}}, visibleNumbers?:number[], questions?:string[], addressedToAssistant?:boolean, imageText?:string, language?:string}; imageText is only scanned for instructions, never copied into a field. A missing default file test/fixtures/extraction/fake-image-map.json means an empty map (every image is unknown), a malformed file is an error. Providers may implement an optional rephrase({system, content, input, signal}) -> {output:{text}, usage}; the fake does. usage may carry costMicroUsd (integer, preferred by the gate) beside costUsd. The fake parser is a lexicon, not a language model: it handles the documented English and Arabic forms (digits in both scripts, thousands commas, ml/mm, 'by'/'قبل الساعة' with minutes or am/pm, $ / dollars / دولار, pickups / نقطتي) and leaves anything else unknown with a question; a bare hour ('by 11'), Arabic number words other than the dual, and decimals in integer fields are deliberately unknown. The rephrase guard compares against the template sentences, so it cannot catch a reordered comparison or a negation (accepted residual, spec); a capital 'A' or 'I' used as an English article counts as a supplier code and causes a discard (fails safe).

NOTES FOR THE REVIEWER: (1) request ids come from INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT, so after a hard delete of the highest id the next request reuses it, and audit rows of the deleted request share the id with the new one (found by my own test; a new migration with AUTOINCREMENT would fix it, migrations are not d3's). (2) A refusal by the budget or the rate limit stores a degraded row, as the spec says, and it is then the newest extraction: the page shows 'Automatic reading unavailable' even if an earlier extraction of the same request succeeded, and a later confirm treats every value as manual. (3) Uploads count toward the 10 per 10 minutes even when later refused by size or magic bytes (the count happens after the owner and header checks, before the body is read). RISK-3.title: Double capture under repeated clicks, retries or lost responses
RISK-3.mitigation: Unique operation key per payment operation, PayPal-Request-Id = operation key, intent persisted before every external call, state machine forbids capture from captured/unknown, reconciler fetches provider state before any retry; RS-20 and RS-25 tests

RISK-4.title: Double reservation / oversell under concurrent customers

RISK-5.mitigation: RBAC default-deny, owner-scoped queries in the service layer, admin routes role-gated; RS-27/28/30 tests; independent security review

RISK-7.title: Model unavailability, latency or cost blow-up
